References and primary documentation

1. References and primary documentation

This reference directory completes the numbered citations used throughout the book. References identify original project manuals, distribution documentation, or primary operational publications. The HarborWorks scenarios, acceptance criteria, and exercises are original teaching examples, not reported production incidents or quoted vendor procedures.

Online documentation may describe a newer release than the teaching baseline. Match the manual to the installed package and distribution before using a directive or option. The Linux man-pages site also hosts manuals supplied by the named upstream projects; consult each page’s colophon for origin and version. Versioned RHEL 9 and OpenSSL 3.0 links are intentional. Documentation was consulted or selected for this instructional edition in September 2026; not every online page or target platform was exhaustively revalidated.

Use man COMMAND, COMMAND --help, package metadata, and the applicable distribution support documentation to settle version-specific behavior. External references are supporting material; the book’s chapter text, worked examples, and core scripts remain readable offline.

SOURCE: EPUB/text/ch040.xhtml — References and primary documentation

2. Read the operational contract

Keep the source procedure, its preconditions and its verification together. Follow the named primary documentation for the installed version. A command copied without its surrounding assumptions answers a different question.

SOURCE: Read the operational contract
